contracts.docstring: Owner group metadata with an optional stable delivery identity for existing clients.
Registered group data; creation replies additionally identify the exact original owner request.
Owner milestone intent; an explicit project scope and stable key enable exact recovery.
Registered milestone data with an original request key only when returning a creation receipt.
Bind owner metadata transactions to the same existing database as the current request.
Create or recover the exact owner group without repeating a committed effect.
Update an epic.
Update supported registered fields without rewriting the original creation receipt.
Retire a manual group atomically while preserving tasks and native history.
Bind owner metadata transactions to the same existing database as the current request.
Create or recover one milestone in its original project and group.
Update a milestone.
Write declared milestone metadata while retaining its immutable original creation response.
Retire a manual milestone only when no native history depends on its identity.
Own group/milestone mutations and their project-scoped receipts in one SQLite transaction.
Reuse the existing source-store transaction boundary without activating a runtime.
Return the exact original resource or atomically persist one new effect and its immutable response.
Create or recover one exact owner group, preserving its original response after later metadata edits.
Write only the group metadata inside its request transaction.
Bind the milestone to the original project/group before creating or recovering its exact receipt.
Reject a removed or foreign parent before writing the milestone in the same transaction.
Retain native task and accepted-plan history while preserving the existing manual in-progress guard.
Remove only a manual group and its milestones atomically, preserving tasks and native plan history.
Remove one manual milestone only after checking its original project and native history under the writer lock.
Restore schema68 atomically only when no planning receipt or later migration exists.
The same owner operation must not duplicate a work group when its original response is unavailable.
The original project/group must retain one milestone when an identical owner request is repeated.
A valid receipt cannot authorize a different group title or be reused for another operation kind.
Identical keys may describe separate projects, but a milestone cannot move its parent into another scope.
Replay returns the original creation receipt while the current resource retains a later owner edit.
Keeping the original receipt prevents replay from recreating a resource the owner subsequently removed.
An actual receipt INSERT failure rolls back the new resource and its audit event before an explicit retry.
Deleting an explicitly chosen manual group detaches its members instead of deleting their work or dependency edges.
Pending child tasks still belong to an accepted plan whose original grouping must remain recoverable.
An explicit unused inverse returns to the exact prior schema and can be upgraded again without changing data.
An original owner receipt must survive an attempted inverse; it cannot be silently reissued later.
Failure after transactional DROP must roll back the infrastructure rather than leave a schema prefix gap.
Deny the final history write after DROP to exercise a real SQLite transactional rollback.
Two actual SQLite writers must converge on the same original resource and immutable receipt.
Release two original writer requests together, then let SQLite serialize their receipt transaction.
Admission protects the grouping; an earlier deletion versions the inputs and rejects the old request without launching an actor.
The actual backup/restore format must retain original identities without re-enrolling execution or recreating metadata.
